methodological_questions: Does a within-game change of the offensive five shift shot-type mix (rim, 3PA, mid-range, FT-generating actions) relative to stints where the five is unchanged?
Can the design separate a personnel effect from shooter, game-state, and coach-selected substitution confounds?
Is the design sensitive enough, at the stated sample size and label quality, to detect a pre-specified minimal shot-mix shift?

historical_evidence.finding: Opponent lineup study (rim big off floor). CHT-075 reports DRIVE +0.82pp (SE 0.25, t=+3.3), POST_UP +0.43pp (SE 0.18), 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31, t=-5.8), PPP +0.008 (SE 0.007, t=+1.1) on N=1.07M possessions. Chat verdict recorded as WEAK/SMALL and not carrying a paper. Limited by small_sample.

PULL_UP exposure-decline diagnostics. Slope with lineup FE -0.0255 (SE 0.0061) shrinks to -0.0063 (SE 0.0036) without lineup FE; same-shooter placebo on other play types -0.0075 (SE 0.0017). Verdict recorded as artifact_found, attributed to a shooter-level confound.

Bonus-threshold and foul-trouble-big adaptation. Bonus FTA +5.08pp is mechanical from the rulebook; DRIVE +0.31pp matches the 2-3 placebo +0.33pp. Foul-trouble-big exposure is 1.44% of possessions because coaches bench the player.

No systematic pivots when a better same-game option exists: 1,466/1,539 (95.3%) had a better option, zero significant pivots in the paper analysis, n=1,539 triggers. Recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null).

Defensive adaptation to repeated play type. League-wide within-game slope -0.0019 PPP/exposure (SE 0.0019); only PULL_UP survives Holm (-0.0243, holm 0.0004). Team-trait split-half r +0.008. Limited by insufficient_exposure, label_or_classification_error, and low_measurement_reliability.

Defensive scheme change using inferred labels: within-game change 61.0%, cross-game 67.7%, transition matrices near-uniform. Doc caveat: the inferred label cannot separate defensive adjustment from offense executing differently.
On-ball scheme labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup/PBP fields: 14.9% labeled for DET and 3.3% for ORL; switches_on field unpopulated. Verdict recorded as failed_gate.

Team heterogeneity in halftime play-type adaptation: heterogeneity variance not above the permutation null (p=0.363); split-half r -0.026 across 120 team-seasons; team-season slope SD 0.6733 vs mean sampling SE 0.6508.
Descriptive play-type mix shifts by halftime margin, crunch time and post-run; no inferential tests; OTHER label known to be noisy (PT audit).
After-timeout play-type shift: POST_UP +2.406 and SPOT_UP +2.333 vs same game-offense-period-minute on 56,423 ATO possessions; half-court PPP -0.0105 (SE 0.0056). Descriptive only.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing a PULL_UP decline with exposure to defensive adaptation using lineup-FE slopes
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact_found: effect shrinks from -0.0255 to -0.0063 without lineup FE, and same-shooter placebo on other play types is of similar size. Limited by confounding.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating bonus-threshold and foul-trouble-big shot-mix changes as strategic adaptation
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: FTA jump is mechanical from the rulebook, DRIVE matches the placebo, and the foul-trouble exposure is too sparse (1.44%) because of coach benching. Limited by insufficient_exposure.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Deriving on-ball coverage labels from NBA matchup/PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as failed_gate: label rates of 14.9% and 3.3%, and switches_on was not populated. Limited by label_or_classification_error and small_sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring defensive scheme changes from play-by-play labels
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable: near-uniform transition matrices consistent with label noise; the label cannot separate defense from offensive execution.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Estimating reliable team-level heterogeneity in play-type adaptation
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable/null: heterogeneity variance is indistinguishable from the permutation null, and split-half reliability is near zero. Limited by low_measurement_reliability.

evidence_establishes: Within this project's records, opponent-lineup changes (SF34) produce detectable group-level shot-mix shifts, for example a 3PA share change of -1.79pp (t=-5.8) on about 1.07M possessions. This is the closest record to a personnel-driven shot-mix effect, though its status is recorded as inconclusive.
Several records show that naive lineup-level or game-state slopes are vulnerable to shooter-level and mechanical confounds (SF-TMP-009, SF-CHT-076), which bears directly on any own-five design.

Label-dependent outcomes (play type, scheme, on-ball coverage) have been unreliable in this project's data (SF-APPS-058, SF-APPA-005, SF-APPM-021), so shot-type mix derived from play-by-play needs an explicit label audit.
Small team-level or lineup-level samples have produced low reliability (SF-TMP-016, SF38), so power must be assessed at the level of the estimand.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests whether changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix. SF34 concerns the opposing lineup, and the positive-control claim in the question is not tested in any record.
No record provides a power calculation for a within-game own-five substitution design; the sample and power field is NOT_RECORDED in several records.
No record establishes the validity of the 2022-23 to 2024-25 derived play-type labels or of substitution-interval reconstruction for this purpose.
No record establishes that a null result would be informative about the design's sensitivity.
own_inferences: The question as posed presupposes its own answer. A positive result would confirm the effect; a null would be ambiguous between no effect and insufficient sensitivity. The test must be framed around a pre-specified minimal detectable effect.

Substitutions are endogenous: coaches sub on matchup, fatigue, foul trouble, score and timeouts, so the shot-mix change after a sub conflates personnel with selection. SF-CHT-076 and SF-TMP-009 show that such selection can produce spurious results.

The 3PA share effect in SF34 (-1.79pp) suggests lineup composition can move shot mix at a magnitude plausibly detectable in a large sample, but this is an inference from an inconclusive record, not an established result.
Within-game own-five changes are probably more frequent than opponent-big-off-floor states, so exposure sparsity may be less severe for this estimand, but this is unverified.
uncertainties: Number of own-five substitution events per season and playoff segment in the stated data is unknown; no count was retrieved.
Whether the rotation intervals and starters files reconstruct the on-court five accurately (including mid-possession changes) is not documented in the retrieved records.
Whether shot-type labels (rim vs mid vs 3PA) from play-by-play are reliable enough for a mix analysis is not established.
Drift across 2022-23 to 2024-25 and between regular season and playoffs is not characterized; the playoff sample is small.
Retrieval returned records but no follow-up tool was called; records were read only from the retrieval snippets, and read_family was not used to check truncated results (for example SF38 and SF34).

historical_effect.explanation: The records changed the decision from a simple 'proceed' to 'proceed_with_changes'. They show that naive lineup and game-state slopes produced artifacts (SF-TMP-009, SF-CHT-076), that derived labels are unreliable (SF-APPS-058, SF-APPA-005), and that small-team samples have low reliability (SF-TMP-016). The design therefore needs placebo substitutions, a label audit and a pre-specified power criterion. The positive-control framing is kept only as a falsifiable test with a minimal effect, not as a presupposed result.

blocking_constraints.text: Substitutions are selected by coaches on game state, fouls, matchups and fatigue; shot-mix changes after a sub may reflect these rather than the personnel change itself (SF-CHT-076, SF-TMP-009).
Own-five changes are non-random; the analysis must condition on the reason for the change or use within-stint placebo substitutions.
Shot-type and play-type labels derived from play-by-play may be noisy (SF-APPM-021 OTHER noise; SF-APPA-005 near-uniform matrices).
Play-type records in the graph database are derived from play-by-play that records outcomes; mix measures can be contaminated by the outcome they are compared with.
Effects of about 1pp need large samples (SF34 used 1.07M possessions); per-team or per-lineup estimates are underpowered (SF-TMP-016).

prior_work.summary: SF34 addresses a related question (opposing rim-big off floor and offensive shot mix) with a recorded 3PA shift and inconclusive status. No retrieved record tests whether changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, so the question as posed is not substantially answered. SF-TMP-009 and SF-CHT-076 show that confounds (shooter FE, mechanical and selection effects) must be addressed before any lineup-level inference.

risks.text: Coach-selected substitutions tied to matchups, fouls and game state; shooter-level confound seen in SF-TMP-009.
Changes made after a poor possession or a foul call may regress toward the mean and produce apparent shot-mix change.
Play-type and shot labels are noisy; OTHER and inferred schemes are not reliable (SF-APPM-021, SF-APPA-005).
Derived play-type records use outcome information, so comparing mix to points risks circularity.
Small effects need large samples; team- and lineup-level estimates have low reliability (SF-TMP-016, SF34).
Shooter or same-lineup placebos can absorb the effect; placebo results in SF-TMP-009 and SF-CHT-076 were close to the main estimate.
Several shot categories and game-state splits generate many comparisons; SF38 survived only one play type under Holm.
Pooling 2022-23 to 2024-25 and playoffs may mix rule and style changes; the playoff sample is small.
Stint-level shot-mix measures may have low reliability at the lineup level (SF38 and SF-TMP-016 show low reliability for team-level measures).

design.estimand: Within-game change in shot-type mix (3PA share primary; rim, mid-range and FT-generating shares secondary) and PPP for possessions after an own-five change (at least two players replaced) relative to matched stints with an unchanged five, conditioned on game state.
design.unit: Possession, with stint boundaries defined by the rotation intervals; comparison pairs formed within game, period and clock window.
design.sample: 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, from the NBA stats play-by-play, rotation intervals and starters files. Exclude bonus and foul-trouble windows, end-of-period and timeout-adjacent possessions as a pre-specified sensitivity analysis. Playoffs reported separately.
design.power: Before any analysis, count own-five change events and compute the SE of the 3PA share change; require the design to detect a pre-specified minimal effect (for example 1pp 3PA share) at 80% power. If power is not met at the stint level, aggregate to team-season or drop the lineup-level estimand.
design.controls: Shooter fixed effects; game, period and clock fixed effects; score margin and possession number; foul counts; timeout indicators; team-season FE; lineup-team-season FE as a sensitivity analysis; a substitution-reason proxy where available. Audit derived play-type labels against raw action type and sub-type on a random sample before use.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo substitutions that leave the five unchanged (bench-for-bench) should show no shot-mix change. (2) Pre-substitution possessions in the same stint window should show no pre-trend. (3) A same-shooter placebo on non-shot outcomes should show no effect. A shot-mix shift that survives only with lineup FE or only in the primary specification counts as an artifact, consistent with SF-TMP-009.
design.multiplicity: Primary outcome fixed as 3PA share; secondary shot shares and PPP corrected by Holm across the pre-specified outcome family.
design.decision_rule: Call the design sensitive only if the placebo substitutions show no effect and the primary 3PA estimate exceeds the pre-specified minimal effect with a CI excluding zero. Report supported only if this holds and the estimate survives the lineup-team-season sensitivity analysis. If the design fails the power check, report untestable. A null with adequate power is reported as rejected; a shift that disappears under placebo is reported as artifact.
design.data_version: NBA stats API play-by-play, rotation intervals and starters files for 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25, regular season and playoffs, as frozen at the 2026-11-02 snapshot; graph-database play-type records are used only after the label audit.

methodological_questions: Can changing the offensive five detectably shift shot mix in play-by-play data?
What confounders and power limits affect a personnel-effect design using substitution intervals?
Which risks (exposure sparsity, selection, derived labels) threaten detecting lineup effects on shot mix?
args.query: offensive lineup change shot mix personnel effect detection substitution rotation intervals NBA play-by-play

You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
